claim.claim-text: displaying content for a first web page in a first pane on a mobile device, the first pane being displayed in a maximized state on the mobile device; receiving a touch input on a navigation control associated with the first pane; and responsive to receiving the touch input, displaying a second web page in a second pane on the mobile device, the second pane being in a minimized state in a dock area, the dock area overlaying the first pane in the maximized state, wherein the minimized state of the second pane displays a smaller version of the second web page than the second pane in a maximized state and wherein the dock area is calculated from a minimum screen coordinate and a dimension of a pane in the minimized state, the dimension being a dimension perpendicular to a scroll direction of the dock area.
2. The method of claim 1, wherein the maximized state of a pane is a largest size of the pane on the mobile device.
3. The method of any of claims 1 or 2, wherein the dock area is proximate a footer area.
4. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the dock area also displays a plurality of web pages in panes in a minimized state, the second web page being one of the plurality of web pages.
5. The method of claim 4, further comprising:
receiving a scroll input on the dock area; and responsive to receiving the scroll input, scrolling the second pane off display and scrolling another of the plurality of web pages on display.
6. The method of any preceding claim, further comprising:
receiving a scroll input of the first pane; and responsive to the scroll input, scrolling the first web page in a direction perpendicular to the dock area.
7. The method of any preceding claim, further comprising:
receiving a command to open a third pane in the dock area; and responsive to receiving the command:
moving the second pane to a new position in the dock area, and opening the third pane in the dock area.
8. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the second web page updates content in parallel with the first web page.
9. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the dock area is horizontally scrollable.
